headline.label: Proposed by phase (Phase 1: 49, Phase 2: 52; overlap not established)

examples.note: Different phase labels are different scopes, not a conflict, but a label alone does not prove the scopes are disjoint: the overlap stays unresolved and no total is formed. The two phases TOGETHER are between 52 (the larger) and 101 (both added); that is a bound on their union, not on the whole scheme, which needs supported common-development membership (E38o) and, for an upper bound, evidence that these phases exhaust it (E38p). Search here is scope-level. A total needs supported non-overlap (E38d).

scope_relations.quote: Phase 1 (plots 1-49) and Phase 2 (plots 50-101) are separate and do not overlap

examples.note: Non-overlap alone: a supported source (a phasing plan, with its literal words) says the phases do not overlap, so the exact sum 101 is the quantity of EXACTLY THESE TWO SCOPES together. It is labelled a combined-scope quantity, search is scope-level, no scalar is cached, and nothing is said about the whole development.

scope_relations.quote: Phase 1 (plots 1-49) and Phase 2 (plots 50-101) are separate and do not overlap

examples.note: Non-overlap plus supported common-development membership: the development is AT LEAST 101 and has no evidenced upper bound, so the sum is still a combined-scope quantity, not the whole-development total (no scalar is cached).

scope_relations.quote: Phase 1 (plots 1-49) and Phase 2 (plots 50-101) are separate and do not overlap
Phases 1 and 2 together are the whole development

examples.note: Non-overlap, common-development membership AND exhaustion are all supported: 101 is an exact whole-development total, the headline drops the "combined scopes" label, search is whole-scheme and certain, and (only here) an exact scalar cache is offered, typed RESOLVED_WHOLE_DEVELOPMENT.

Approved 49 with a later proposed revision of 52. At a minimum of 50 only the proposed basis meets the filter; with a range of 10 to 50 only the approved basis does; the result names the basis either way. Meeting a size filter is not a confirmed quantity, a planning approval or a buyer fit.
Revised approval: permission 2 states it supersedes permission 1; the 49 is preserved as historical evidence.

examples.proposal: OUTLINE PERMISSION FOR UP TO 50 DWELLINGS
examples.note: A qualified approved maximum keeps its qualifier everywhere and routes to assessment. "Up to 50" has no evidenced positive lower bound, so it can be anything from 0 to 50: it is only a possible size match for 10-100 and even for 1-100, and meets only a range that starts at 0. See E38q for a separately supported minimum.

9 versus 12 crosses the 10+ threshold: a possible size match, listed separately from matches that meet the filter, routed to assessment. Against 5-20 both figures lie inside, so it meets that filter (the quantity is still under review).
A form or proposal alone cannot establish an approved count: the claimed approval is recorded as unsupported and the supported proposed quantity is shown.
Alternative permissions are preserved side by side; the larger or the later does not replace the other.
The later document does not supersede the earlier one: without an explicit relationship the conflict stays unresolved.
Dwelling count, planning status and construction progress are three separate facts; none changes another.
Size eligibility is only the size gate: a refused application still has a supported proposed quantity of 49; the status gate is separate and not decided here.

headline.label: Proposed by phase (Phase 1: 49, Phase 2: 52; overlap not established)

examples.note: Claimed non-overlap and common-development membership with no supporting source or words are ignored. The union of the two phases is bounded by 52 and 101, but with no supported membership there is NO whole-scheme claim at all: each phase is judged on its own, the result is labelled scope-level and names the phase that earns it (Phase 1 alone for a maximum of 51). The sum is not offered as the scheme.

headline.label: Proposed by phase (Phase 1: 49, Phase 2: 52; overlap not established)

examples.note: With supported common-development membership the whole scheme is at least 52 (the larger phase) and, because nothing says these two phases exhaust the development, has NO evidenced upper bound: 101 is not offered as one (a range with any maximum is only a possible match; a maximum below 52 cannot match).
